$comment: Canonical slide design canvases — the single source of truth for both the
static guard (scripts/lint-css.mjs, rules 0 and 4) and the runtime geometry
guard (scripts/check-canvas.ts).
"canvases" is the declared list. Every id in it MUST have a sibling block
of the same name with a positive integer width and height. A template opts
in to a canvas with `canvases: [...]` in its config.yaml; when that key is
absent the template is taken to declare "defaultCanvases" below, so the 46
templates that pre-date the third canvas stay valid with no edit.
These canvases are HALF of a cross-repo contract; the other half is
"counterparts" below. Every copy must describe the same numbers.
Enforcement is deliberately asymmetric:
- The BLOCKING comparison runs in dfl-lesson-studio
(scripts/check-canvas-contract.mjs). It can fetch this file
unauthenticated because this repo is public; the reverse is not
possible without exposing a token to a public repo.
- This repo LEADS. A canvas change lands here first (config + rescaling
every template in one PR, as #69 did); dfl-lesson-studio follows with a
constant change and is red until it does. A blocking gate on both sides
would deadlock the first half of any canvas change.
- dfl-render (dfl-services:services/dfl-render/src/lib/capture-slide.ts)
held a THIRD, undeclared copy of these numbers until 2026-08-26, with
nothing scanning it. It is listed below so the copy is inside the
contract rather than beside it.
What this repo can verify locally — and does, as rule 0 of lint-css.mjs —
is that every declared canvas is well-formed, that the landscape/portrait
PAIR is still a transpose (dfl-lesson-studio derives portrait that way), and
that the counterpart block is still here. Note that the transpose rule is a
property of that ONE pair, not of the canvas list: social-portrait is 4:5
and transposes nothing.
fluidTemplates are the ONLY templates allowed to size to their container
instead of a fixed canvas. It is a local decision with no counterpart in
the app, and is NOT part of the contract. Keep the list tiny and justified —
each entry needs a rationale below.

canvasRationale.landscape: The 16:9 lesson/deck canvas. Every template declares it.
canvasRationale.portrait: 9:16, landscape transposed. The vertical lesson canvas; dfl-lesson-studio derives it from LANDSCAPE_WIDTH/HEIGHT rather than storing it.
canvasRationale.social-portrait: 1080x1350, 4:5 — the Instagram portrait post. It is NOT a transpose of anything, which is why rule 0 checks well-formedness per canvas and the transpose only for the landscape/portrait pair. OPT-IN per template (config.yaml `canvases:`): a mandatory third canvas would cost an HTML, a CSS and a golden PNG across all 46 templates for no gain. Plan 20260822-branded-image-templates-deterministic-mcp, ADR-8.

fluidRationale.blank: The 'screen + webcam only' recording backdrop. It must stretch to whatever surface the recorder hands it, so width/height:100% is deliberate. See ADR-1 of plan 20260430-lesson-studio-ai-mode-ux-fixes.
